A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Muon-based INR study. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original image and audio fitting, shape representation, CT reconstruction, super-resolution, and NeRF experiments in Tables 1–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and reports additional optimizer comparisons, sensitivity analyses, and results aggregated across multiple seeds.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure remains hybrid Muon/Adam optimization: Newton–Schulz orthogonalization for hidden weight matrices and Adam for input/output weights, biases, and other parameters. GA-Planes experiments apply this existing rule to another architecture without introducing a new optimization component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Kodak and AFHQ images, Bach and counting audio, the shortened audio excerpt, Armadillo and Thai Statue, the same CT image and DIV2K example, and eight synthetic NeRF scenes. V2's 'additional' NeRF scenes were already in v1 Table 6; new architecture and sensitivity experiments retain existing task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds Lion alongside Adam and Muon in the Kodak comparison (Tables 18–19), introduces GA-Planes Sum/Multiply optimizer comparisons (Table 22), and expands the explicitly compared BatchNorm and pretraining variants (Figure 2 and Table 14). These substantially broaden the comparison methods.

E3.justification: Most existing budgets, metrics, and data protocols remain unchanged, but selected audio, SDF, and SISR learning rates change. Table 12 now selects stable second-best SISR configurations after divergence across seeds. Added supplementary protocols sweep Fourier-feature sigma and decoder widths of 32, 64, and 128 under specified controls.

E4.justification: V2 adds a Lion optimizer ablation, Fourier-feature sensitivity tests, and GA-Planes feature-combination and decoder-capacity analyses (Appendix D). It also quantifies and expands the existing rank-preserving intervention comparison. The 200 ms audio ablation is retained from v1 Appendix C.3 and moved to D.2, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V1 explicitly reports best single runs for CT, SISR, and NeRF and lacks seed uncertainty for audio and SDF. V2 newly reports mean and standard deviation over five seeds for audio, CT, and SISR, and three seeds for SDF and NeRF, plus seed information for ablations. Kodak's across-image standard deviations already appeared in v1.

E6.justification: Most main benchmark tables replace individual results with seed aggregates, and substantial comparison and ablation results are added. For example, CT FINER Adam/Muon PSNR changes from 32.13/31.65 best-single values to 31.93 ± 0.50/32.92 ± 0.21 five-seed means. Successful SIREN/FINER SDF results replace v1's failure account. These are revised reported outcomes, not direct version-to-version performance gains; Kodak Table 1 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 extends the layer-level derivation to include affine biases and their gradients, explaining why they do not alter the stated row-space inclusion. The principal stable-rank definition, gradient-rank inequality, and orthogonalization result remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the claimed improvement from up to 9 dB over the previous state of the art to improvement over the same architecture; the NeRF discussion makes the same qualification. The central rank-preservation and optimizer contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's brief caution that Muon may not be optimal, v2 explicitly argues that high stable rank alone is insufficient and develops interpretations of the encoding and decoder analyses. New Section 5 distinguishes diagnostic rank bounds from optimal-rank or trajectory predictions and discusses approximation and tuning limitations. The earlier interpretation that positional encoding is unnecessary for Muon-based SDF fitting is removed.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B largely retain their implementation details. V2 adds GA-Planes encoder/decoder descriptions, parameter-group learning rates, and controlled capacity-sweep details, and updates selected learning-rate configurations. The project/code pointer changes from muon-inrs.github.io to rank-inrs.github.io.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Chng et al. (2025) and discusses curvature-aware preconditioning as complementary prior work. New citations also support Lion, GA-Planes, matrix-sign approximations, and rank-based analysis. The overall research positioning remains similar; publication updates to existing references do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: Most original prose and section order are retained. V2 locally expands the rank argument and related work, rewrites the conclusion, introduces separate Limitations and Ablations sections, and relocates the existing audio ablation. Author, affiliation, and publication-header text also changes.

P2.justification: Figure 2 changes from a four-panel grid to an eight-panel comparison with metrics, and the SDF illustration is replaced. CT/SISR tables become full-width uncertainty displays; the original NeRF table is split across Tables 6, 16, and 17. Several new analysis tables substantially expand the visual presentation, while most other qualitative figures are retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses v1's reliance on best single-run results through broad seed-based uncertainty reporting and adds controls that test optimizer specificity, encoding sensitivity, and decoder capacity. Narrower performance claims and substantive limitations improve interpretation. Unexplained differences between duplicated Kodak Muon scores remain—for example, SIREN PSNR is 41.43 in Table 1 versus 42.33 in Table 19—but this reporting weakness does not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support and qualification.
